extracted.intended_audience: first-time grant writers and applicants (nonprofits, small businesses, organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for planning, drafting, and submitting a grant proposal that follows the funder's RFP and includes required supporting documents and a budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the grant application carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight all questions you must answer and materials you have to include. Underline key words or phrases you might want to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the application as your checklist; note required attachments, formats, and any specific terminology the funder uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the grant's purpose and match your organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the purpose the grant is intended to fulfill and make sure to highlight your organization's contribution to this purpose, both in the past and in the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect your program activities and track record to the funder's stated goals so reviewers see alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brainstorm organizational strengths and arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you start writing—brainstorm. What are the strong points of your organization? Your program? What are your best arguments and examples?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these ideas as the basis for persuasive examples and evidence in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a one-paragraph summary statement (executive summary/abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by writing a one-paragraph description of your request that includes who you are, what your project is, how much you’re asking for, and exactly what you'll use the money for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This big-picture summary can serve as an abstract or the opening of your narrative; ensure it reflects the final proposal after revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an outline that follows the RFP
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an outline describing each step of your plan and organize your thinking. Use the grantor's request for proposals (RFP) or criteria as the basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outline should follow, painstakingly, the sequence and terms prescribed by the grantor; expand each point as needed to fully explain each section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm the proposal is the kind of project the grantor funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if your proposal is the type of project the grantor actually funds; don't assume money equals fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders are usually specific and rarely deviate from their category; if your project falls outside their scope, don't apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write an initial draft to capture ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the first draft—get your ideas down on paper; it doesn't have to look good initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with questions you have the most answers for; if stuck, move to another section. Expect multiple rewrites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize aspects the funder values
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on parts of your project that the funder will like—use their guidelines for clues (e.g., environmental responsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make relevant features stand out and highlight partnerships where appropriate to build credibility and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe clear, specific goals and uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly lay out specific goals: describe what the money will be used for, with concrete, specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague statements; give measurable, concrete outcomes (example: buy two new computers and create two part-time paid staff positions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish and revise for clarity and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the draft shine by carefully polishing: ensure ideas are clear and delivery is concise; read out loud to check flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite several times, use the key words/phrases from the application where appropriate, and verify the summary matches the final proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the funder's rules exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the proposal and the requirements; every grant has rules and procedures that must be followed exactly as written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it says submit via the online form, don't send it another way; failure to follow rules may disqualify your application before review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread carefully and use multiple proofreaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread for spelling, typing, and grammatical errors and have at least two people proofread your proposal before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read aloud, use other techniques (some read backwards) to catch mistakes—aim to submit a flawless document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do a reality check with outsiders
rubrics_metrics.description: Have at least two people outside your organization or discipline read the proposal and then ask them questions about your concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outsiders cannot explain what you intend, reviewers likely won't either—clarity for non-experts is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the project's budget using accurate numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't guess about the numbers; research and evaluate the actual expenses you will incur. Use real numbers, not rounded estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid estimates that end in large round numbers (e.g., 000.00). Inaccurate financials undermine credibility and can cost you the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce a detailed budget summary with categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a budget summary that categorizes personnel expenses and other costs (salary/fringes, purchased services, supplies, occupancy, communications, travel, equipment, printing, capital, indirect costs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically allocate across columns: total project cost, amount sought from funder, and matching funds. Showing applicant stake increases competitiveness. Do not use 'other expenses' without a full explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a budget justification that explains numerically how you arrived at the amounts in the budget summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all amounts balance and that numbers are consistent throughout the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document partnerships and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that your participation matters via letters of support, newspaper articles, and other documentation of success and partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents establish validity and strengthen credibility with reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include other required supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Add required documents such as a 501(c)(3) letter of tax-exemption, an audit or financial report, and a list of the board of directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a file with several copies of each so you can include them as required by different funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add a strong cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter summarizing your request, the project's purpose, the amount requested, and a list of the proposal contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover letter often provides the funder’s first impression—invest as much care in it as in the rest of the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-check, make copies, and meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Double check that you've answered all questions, included required materials, make a copy for your files, and ensure timely delivery to meet the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late or incomplete applications look sloppy and may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up appropriately after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: About a week after mailing, call to make sure the application arrived and is complete, and keep the grantor informed of major successes during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use follow-up as an opportunity to confirm completeness and to share significant updates (press coverage, achievements); also be patient—the review process can take a long time.

rubrics_metrics.name: General process tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to several sources, avoid shortcuts, and give yourself enough time to prepare a strong proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because any single grant is uncertain, submit multiple applications; a well-prepared package requires time and care.
